title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' cycle. The objects are:
- the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free profinite on two generators;
- an extension Ĝ^+_{0,3} containing π̂_{0,3}. It carries 'half-loop' elements ε_0, ε_1 with squares l_0 = ε_0^2 and l_1 = ε_1^2, and symmetry elements ρ (order 2) and σ_∞ (order 3).
- a homomorphism φ̂ : π̂_{0,3} → Ĝ^+_{0,3}, sending the loop l_0 to the half-loop ε_0. It behaves like a degree-2 'square-root' comparison map between the group and an index-2 or orbifold version of itself.
- M^{!~}_{0,3}: a group of automorphisms satisfying the 'loop condition' (à lacets).
- N^{!~}_{0,3}: the corresponding group of exterior automorphisms.
- L_0: the inertia (loop) subgroup generated by l_0.

Automorphisms are parametrised by 'special' triples (α, β, f), written u_{(α,β,f)}. By formula (19) of the previous page, u_{ξ,f} = int(f^{-1}) u_ξ. Here u_ξ is defined by u_ξ(ρ) = ξρ and u_ξ(σ_∞) = (ξ l_1^{-ν})^{(…)} σ_∞, with ξ subject to conditions (14) and (15) (dihedral and cyclic relations of Grothendieck–Teichmüller type). Corollary 3 characterised the u_ξ as the automorphisms that commute with φ̂ and normalise L_0.

This page proves the triple version of that characterisation.
- Normalising L_0 forces f = l_0^n.
- Commuting with φ̂ means that λ in formula (6) with r = 0 equals 1. Here λ = φ̂(f)^{-1} f (21), so the condition is φ̂(f) = f (22).
- For f = l_0^n this reads ε_0^n = l_0^n = ε_0^{2n}, hence ε_0^n = 1. So n = 0 and f = 1, and u = u_{(α,β,1)} = u_ξ with ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1}.

Corollary 4. The normalised u_ξ form a subgroup M^{!≈}_{0,3}(ω) of Norm_{M^{!~}}(L_0). This subgroup meets the inner automorphisms (the image of π̂_{0,3}) only in {1}. Its image in N^{!~}_{0,3} is the subgroup N^{!≈}_{0,3}: exterior loop-automorphisms of Ĝ^+_{0,3} that stabilise π̂_{0,3} and with which φ̂ commutes exteriorly. Hence formula (23) gives an isomorphism {u_ξ | ξ solution of (14), (15)} ≅ N^{!≈}_{0,3}.

The next page checks the trivial-intersection claim and concludes there is a canonical partial section of M^{!~} → N^{!~} over N^{!≈}.

In modern terms, this is the familiar procedure of lifting outer Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type automorphisms of F̂_2 to genuine automorphisms by a normalisation, here 'fix the inertia at 0 up to conjugacy class'. It is analogous to Drinfeld's normal form (λ, f) acting by x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f^{-1} y^λ f. The extra condition of compatibility with a degree-2 map φ̂ singles out a subgroup.
errors: Deducing n = 0 from ε_0^n = 1 (n in Ẑ) tacitly uses that ε_0 has infinite (profinite) order generating a copy of Ẑ in Ĝ^+. This is plausible but not stated.
The trivial intersection with inner automorphisms is asserted here but only verified on the next page. That verification contains a notational slip, 'ε_1^{2n} = 0' written for = 1.

ideas.what: Normalised lift of exterior automorphisms: among automorphisms normalising the inertia subgroup L_0 and commuting with φ̂, the conjugating element f must be trivial. This gives a canonical section over a subgroup of outer automorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Normalised representatives of GT-type outer automorphisms (Drinfeld normalisation, f in the commutator subgroup)
ideas.where_published: Only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the detailed computations are unpublished

ideas.what: Characterising the subgroup N^{!≈} of exterior loop-automorphisms of the extension Ĝ^+_{0,3} that commute exteriorly with a 'half-loop' homomorphism φ̂ : π̂_{0,3} → Ĝ^+_{0,3} (l_0 ↦ ε_0, with l_0 = ε_0^2). It is shown isomorphic to the set of solutions ξ of the loop equations (14), (15).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of GT-type actions with degree-2 covers / orbifold quotients (cf. Nakamura–Schneps, Lochak–Schneps on dihedral or level-2 structures)
ideas.where_published: Possibly anticipated in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), unpublished until recently

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly constructs a canonical partial section of the automorphism group over the subgroup of exterior automorphisms compatible with a degree-2 'half-loop' map φ̂. He identifies that subgroup with solutions of his loop equations, a refinement of the GT-type group cut out by a φ̂-compatibility condition. The precise relation to later level-2 or dihedral variants of GT is not clear from this page alone.
missed.quote: Les u_ξ normalisés forment un sous-groupe de Norm_{M^{!~}_{0,3}}(L_0) ... dont l'intersection avec π̂_{0,3} est réduite à {1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could document an early, independent formulation of a φ̂-compatible subgroup of GT. Its main value is historical, unless the subgroup N^{!≈} differs from known variants.

deep.surprise_reason: The step is a technical normalisation lemma within Grothendieck's own GT-type framework. The mathematics, canonical normalised lifts, is standard in later GT theory. Only the specific φ̂-compatibility setting is mildly interesting historically.
transcription_corrections: '(qui expriment la commutation de normalisation L_0)' should read '(qui expriment la condition de normaliser L_0)'.
'doit égal à 1' should read 'doit être égal à 1' (or 'doit égaler 1').
In 'ε_0^n = l_0^n', the annotation ε_0^{2n} is written under l_0^n as its value; it is not a separate factor.
The left-margin note 'le s-groupe N^{!≈}_{0,3}' is an insertion into the sentence about the image in N^{!~}_{0,3}.
The equation number at the bottom is (23), overwritten.
